negative_control.declaration: With the abbreviation lookup removed from _record_carried_head, the nine-character case in tests/test_reclaimed_run_review_head.py fails because the head resolves to the repository HEAD rather than the run's commit.

node_definition.done_when: The plan section crew-runtime-positive-controls §34 is the authority; read it first. In reckon/crew/recovery.py, _record_carried_head resolves an abbreviated commits: entry (seven or more hex characters) to its full object id through the run's repository, by running git rev-parse --verify on the entry with ^{commit} appended, and still skips an entry git cannot resolve unambiguously. For a run whose worktree path no longer exists, where neither the manifest's commits nor the pointer's head resolves, _review_head_and_tree returns an empty head instead of the repository HEAD. The review reflex then composes no review for that run, and the reason it records names the missing head. tests/test_reclaimed_run_review_head.py builds a temporary git repository with two commits, a pointer whose worktree path does not exist, and a manifest naming the run's commit by a nine-character id. It asserts _run_head_for_review returns that commit's full id, and that the id differs from the repository's HEAD after a later commit lands on it. A second case gives a manifest with no commits and a pointer with no head, and asserts the reflex composes nothing and names the missing head. Existing tests that reach _review_head_and_tree, _run_head_for_review or _record_carried_head keep passing; grep tests/ for those names to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-runtime-positive-controls/reclaimed-run-review-keys-on-its-own-head.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
